title: Container and pod security: security context, admission and Pod Security Standards

videos.script: A container is a process on the node, with some walls around it. How high those walls are is written in the pod, and the defaults are lower than most people expect. {{walls}} By default the process runs as root, holds a dozen kernel capabilities, and can write anywhere in its own filesystem. {{defaults}} The security context is where you raise the walls: another user, no capabilities, a read-only filesystem. {{context}} But a setting in a pod only protects the pods that remember it. So the second half of this lesson is about refusing the pods that forget, at the door, before they ever run. {{door}} Pod Security Standards do that per namespace, with three levels. And a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy lets you write a rule of your own. {{rules}}
